Getting started

Device and network: make your existing computer usable

If your computer can run the tools you choose, start there. When choosing a Mac, check the software’s current operating-system and chip requirements. Add memory, storage, or another display when your projects and actual working conditions warrant them. Starting with cloud models does not require a GPU for training large models locally, or reproducing the author’s desktop.

Your network needs to support sign-in, documentation, dependency downloads, and uploads. If your connection needs proxy configuration, the Clash Verge Rev project repository is a verifiable client source. It manages network configurations; it does not supply a network service or a model account. You still need your own usable, trusted configuration. DuyaoSS can serve as a community reference for provider introductions, speed-test records, and routing explainers; some visible test and review samples date from 2018–2024, and the site says promotional information may not be updated in time. Treat it as a lead: check providers’ current terms and routes, then test with your own carrier, region, and device. An individual review cannot guarantee performance on your current connection. Installing a client alone does not establish connectivity.

For readers living mainly in mainland China, distinguish network connectivity from service availability. Mainland China is absent from OpenAI’s ChatGPT supported-region list. A proxy client does not change that service condition. Establish which services and accounts are actually available to you before selecting tools; the practice described here can also develop with another available model.

When proxy traffic is limited or large software, dependency packages, and Docker images download slowly, ask the model to inspect suitable mirrors and caches. Package sources and Docker image registries are different configuration targets. A directly reachable mirror can reduce proxy traffic, while caching reduces repeated downloads. Docker's registry-mirror documentation describes fetching from upstream when needed and reusing cached content afterward. Check origin, supported packages or registries, synchronization, versions, and integrity information, then test on the current network. Keep usable caches rather than repeatedly clearing and downloading them.

From a subscription to global instructions and essential Skills

Web ChatGPT provides a cloud conversation and tool space for discussion, research, understanding materials, and developing ideas. With the relevant access, local Codex can directly help construct and maintain a personal knowledge and working environment: connecting materials, notes, applications, files, scripts, tools, and configuration, and turning ideas into usable arrangements. A project folder is one working location within it; the environment itself can be an ongoing object of improvement. You bring purpose, experience, and judgment; the model carries explanation, investigation, construction, execution, and checking. A concrete need can begin that collaboration.

If you have no usable account, establish connectivity, then choose and purchase a subscription actually available to you. Start on the Web and ask the model to help articulate your purpose and global instructions. Follow the official quickstart to download a local client, sign in, and connect a working directory. An existing local client can also help with these preparations.

Check whether your existing account includes the Codex capabilities, limits, and client you need. The official documentation states that Codex is included in ChatGPT plans; actual capabilities and limits depend on the plan, account, and rollout. Use the sign-in guidance for ChatGPT-account access. If your current entitlement fits, you do not need a duplicate “Codex subscription.” Compare an upgrade only after a concrete limit or missing feature becomes relevant.

Choose a stable personal subscription, then compare its practical value

Prefer an individual consumer (ToC) subscription, and put reliability ahead of discounts. Establish account ownership, continued sign-in, the models and usage actually available, and renewal and recovery arrangements. Prefer direct official purchase or a clearly sourced channel with dependable delivery and renewal. A short-term discount does not compensate for repeated failures, reclaimed accounts, or an inability to renew. Compare business (ToB) team or enterprise plans when you actually need collaboration, organization management, enterprise data policies, or contractual guarantees; an enterprise label alone does not make a plan better for an individual.

Build everyday collaboration around one stable primary subscription, using its actual included entitlements across the local CLI/app and the Web. Make the arrangement useful before adding or switching subscriptions for a demonstrated capability difference. Frequent switching creates adaptation work for instructions, Skills, interfaces, and habits. Reassess before renewal: continuity does not mean permanent lock-in. Interfaces for a specific purpose, such as translation, can still be configured separately.

Among candidates with adequate reliability and capabilities, assess local and Web use together and use the corresponding models' API prices as a reference for subscription value:

  1. List capabilities you will actually use. Check the models, modes, tools, limits, and reset periods available locally and on the Web. Count shared allowances once; two interfaces do not imply two allowances.
  2. Estimate the API alternative for comparable work. Where a comparable API exists, estimate monthly input, cached input, output, and necessary tool usage against the provider's current rates. The OpenAI API pricing page, for example, identifies billable categories. An expensive model you never use adds no practical value. Compare Web-only capabilities or unobservable usage separately rather than inventing a precise conversion.
  3. Compare the actual monthly fee with work you can reliably complete. Account for local plus Web demand, quality, speed, allowances, and renewal cost, then choose the better value among dependable candidates. API replacement cost is a comparison reference, not a way to derive an included token allowance by dividing the subscription fee by a token price. A higher API price does not automatically make a subscription more worthwhile.

ChatGPT and the API have separate billing. A subscription is not an API balance, and an API balance does not replace a subscription. Explore API billing when you actually build your own API application or choose API authentication. Consult current official prices and availability rather than treating this guide as a fixed shopping list.

Let the model help establish the working arrangement

Begin global instructions with a few arrangements that apply across your work: how you want to participate, what the model should carry, how native language and English are used, where files and results belong, and how the model completes work and makes it visible. A Web model can help write them; a local model can place them where the actual client reads them and check that they take effect. You provide purposes and corrections without having to maintain a whole instruction system yourself. Instructions evolve through use.

Ask the model to select, download, and verify the Skills needed now from trustworthy sources. Initial capabilities might cover research, local environment diagnosis, scripts and tools, document reading, interface implementation, versioning, and publication. Choose packages supported by the actual client and check origin, compatibility, and invocation rather than filling a skill store. Agent Skills explains this capability-package format.

Form settings that fit through actual work

Tell the model what you want to do now, where the relevant materials are, and your preferences for language, explanation, responsibilities, and presentation. For example: “Discuss this with me in Chinese, make this material comfortable to read, retain its sources, and check the links.” Working context and preferences can develop task by task. Let the model maintain them in suitable instructions or project notes, and test their fit through use and correction.

Writing a personal philosophy is difficult, long-term work. Begin tool use by completing a real task and improving the environment through its results. Philosophy authoring, a complete personal profile, five core accounts, and a personal website are not preparation steps. If the background interests you, select Yinyang's methods and material around a question; that reading and the current tool setup serve their respective purposes.

Make Skills discoverable and composable in Chinese

Begin each Skill's description with a short Chinese name and purpose, while retaining its exact native English identifier. You can then express ordinary Chinese intentions and let the model discover, select, read, and invoke suitable capabilities currently available, without memorizing technical English names. The Chinese description supports understanding and discovery; the native identifier still supports accurate installation, invocation, and updates.

Distinguish origin by beginning user-authored descriptions with 用户自制：. Skills obtained from external repositories or plugins can begin directly with their Chinese name and purpose. For example, a user-authored description could read “用户自制：资料整理：整理选定材料并保留来源。” and an external one “PDF 阅读：读取和检查 PDF 文档。”. Translation or local adaptation does not by itself change authorship. Have the model check descriptions in the maintained source and the client's discovery list so they survive updates.

Give preference to user-authored methods that fit your purpose, and actively combine related methods as connected working capabilities. They can contribute while understanding a need, configuring the environment, doing the work, and revising the result. Combine suitable external specialists where they help. Priority follows the task, scope, and fit.

Use the available capabilities to complete actual work next. Search for and connect tools when needed, writing a new implementation only when a suitable one is missing. Your working arrangement develops through purpose, use, and feedback.
